method_card.title: School Life, Rules and Issues
method_card.content:
This lesson covers school facilities, rules using modal verbs, uniform descriptions with accusative adjective endings, and school issues such as stress and bullying.

GermanEnglish
das Klassenzimmerclassroom
die Kantinecanteen
die Bibliotheklibrary
die Turnhallegymnasium
der Schulhofschool yard
man mussyou must / one must
man darf nichtyou must not / one is not allowed to
man sollyou should / one should
die Schuluniformschool uniform
tragento wear
das Mobbingbullying
der Stressstress
der Prüfungsdruckexam pressure
Ich denke, dass...I think that...
hässlich / praktischugly / practical

Grammar focus 1 — modal verbs for rules: Man muss / soll / darf nicht + infinitive at end. The modal sits at position 2; the infinitive goes to the clause end. Example: Man muss die Schuluniform tragen. Never put the infinitive immediately after the modal as in English ('Man muss tragen die Uniform' is wrong).

Grammar focus 2 — accusative adjective endings after uniform: Tragen (to wear) takes the accusative case. After einen/eine/ein, adjective endings are: masculine -en (einen roten Rock), feminine -e (eine blaue Hose), neuter -es (ein weißes Hemd), plural -e (schwarze Schuhe).

Grammar focus 3 — dass clauses: Like weil and obwohl, the conjunction dass sends the verb to the end: Ich denke, dass die Schuluniform bequem ist.

Model paragraph: In meiner Schule gibt es eine Kantine und eine große Bibliothek. Man muss die Schuluniform tragen. Ich trage eine blaue Jacke, ein weißes Hemd und schwarze Schuhe. Ich denke, dass die Schuluniform praktisch ist, obwohl sie manchmal unbequem ist.
(In my school there is a canteen and a large library. You must wear school uniform. I wear a blue blazer, a white shirt and black shoes. I think that school uniform is practical, although it is sometimes uncomfortable.)
steps: Learn school facility vocabulary with es gibt (die Kantine, die Bibliothek, die Turnhalle)
Express rules with man muss / darf nicht / soll + infinitive at the end of the clause
Describe uniform using tragen + accusative adjective endings (-en masc., -e fem., -es neut.)
Give opinions using Ich denke/glaube/finde, dass + verb at the end
Discuss school issues (Mobbing, Stress, Prüfungsdruck) with opinion structures

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — school rules and uniform appear regularly in 50-word writing tasks and speaking conversations

worked_examples.question: How do you describe school uniform using accusative adjective endings?

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Use tragen (to wear). It requires the accusative case — the article changes for masculine nouns.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Accusative adjective endings: masculine einen roten Rock, feminine eine blaue Hose, neuter ein weißes Hemd, plural schwarze Schuhe.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Ich trage einen roten Rock, eine blaue Hose, ein weißes Hemd und schwarze Schuhe.

worked_examples.question: How do dass clauses work? Show with an example about school uniform.

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Dass (that) is a subordinating conjunction. Like weil and obwohl, it sends the conjugated verb to the end of the clause.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Opinion verbs before dass: Ich denke (I think), Ich finde (I find), Ich glaube (I believe).

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Ich denke, dass die Schuluniform wichtig ist. — The verb ist moves to the end after dass.

bronze.question: Match the German school facility words to the English meaning
Match the German uniform and rules vocabulary to the English meaning
Complete the school rule sentence — modal verb + infinitive at end

gaps.correct_explain: After darf nicht, the infinitive goes to the end: Man darf nicht laufen.

wrong.läuft: läuft is the conjugated er/sie form. After a modal verb, use the infinitive: laufen.
wrong.gelaufen: gelaufen is the past participle. After a modal verb, use the infinitive: laufen.

bronze.question: Complete the sentence with the correct accusative adjective ending

gaps.correct_explain: After einen (masculine accusative), the adjective takes -en: einen roten Rock.

wrong.e: -e is the feminine ending. Rock is masculine (der Rock): use -en.
wrong.es: -es is the neuter ending. Rock is masculine: use -en.

gaps.correct_explain: After eine (feminine accusative), the adjective takes -e: eine blaue Hose.

wrong.en: -en is the masculine accusative ending. Hose is feminine (die Hose): use -e.

bronze.question: What does 'Man darf im Gebäude kein Handy benutzen' mean?
options: You must not use a mobile phone in the building
You must use a mobile phone in the building
You should use a mobile phone in the building
You can use a mobile phone in the building

bronze.question: What does 'Ich denke, dass die Krawatte hässlich ist' mean?
options: I think that the tie is ugly
I think that the tie is beautiful
I believe the tie is expensive

silver.question: Complete the sentence (no word bank)
silver.english: I **think** that school uniform is practical because everyone looks the **same**.
sentence_parts: , dass die Schuluniform praktisch ist, weil alle

gaps.correct_explain: denke (think), finde (find) or glaube (believe) all work here to introduce a dass clause.

wrong.denkt: denkt is the er/sie form. For ich, use denke.

gaps.correct_explain: gleich means 'the same'. Aussehen is a separable verb: the prefix aus- moves to the end, so gleich aussehen is correct.

silver.question: Find and fix the grammatical error
silver.explanation: After einen (masculine accusative), the adjective must end in -en: einen blauen Rock.

silver.question: Build the sentence in German
silver.english: You must be quiet in lessons.

distractor_labels.muss: muss (must) is a stronger obligation than soll (should). Both are grammatically valid here, but soll is used in the model answer.

silver.source_text: I wear a white shirt and a red tie. I think that the uniform is ugly.
model_answers: Ich trage ein weißes Hemd und eine rote Krawatte. Ich denke, dass die Uniform hässlich ist.
hints: I think that = Ich denke, dass

gold.question: Build the sentence in German
gold.english: In Great Britain you must wear school uniform.

distractor_labels.trägt: wrong form — after muss, use the infinitive tragen at the end, not the conjugated form trägt
distractor_labels.soll: soll (should) is a weaker obligation than muss (must). The sentence says 'must', so use muss.

gold.question: Role Play
gold.scenario: Your German exchange partner asks you about your school, its facilities, the rules and the school uniform.

bullets.prompt: Describe your school and its facilities using es gibt.
bullets.model_answer: Meine Schule ist groß. Es gibt eine Kantine, eine Bibliothek und eine Turnhalle, aber es gibt kein Fitness-Studio.
bullets.note: es gibt + accusative, aber + kein (negation of noun), school size adjective

bullets.prompt: Tell them two school rules using modal verbs.
bullets.model_answer: Man muss im Unterricht leise sein und man darf im Gang nicht laufen.
bullets.note: man muss/darf nicht + infinitive at end of clause

bullets.prompt: Describe your uniform and give your opinion using a dass clause.
bullets.model_answer: Ich trage einen schwarzen Rock, ein weißes Hemd und eine blaue Krawatte. Ich finde, dass die Uniform hässlich aber praktisch ist.
bullets.note: accusative adjective endings, dass + verb at end

bullets.prompt: Compare school in Germany and Great Britain regarding uniform.
bullets.model_answer: In Deutschland trägt man keine Schuluniform, aber in Großbritannien muss man die Uniform tragen. Ich denke, dass das besser ist.
bullets.note: cultural comparison, man + kein, dass + verb at end

gold.audio_text: Ich trage eine blaue Jacke, ein weißes Hemd und schwarze Schuhe. Ich denke, dass die Schuluniform bequem ist, obwohl sie teuer ist.
gold.correct_text: Ich trage eine blaue Jacke, ein weißes Hemd und schwarze Schuhe. Ich denke, dass die Schuluniform bequem ist, obwohl sie teuer ist.

gold.question: Complete the sentence (no word bank — Higher: dass + obwohl nested clauses)
gold.english: I believe that school uniform is important because everyone looks the **same**, although it is sometimes **uncomfortable**.
sentence_parts: Ich glaube, dass die Schuluniform wichtig ist, weil alle gleich aussehen, obwohl sie manchmal

gaps.correct_explain: unbequem means uncomfortable — the negative form of bequem (comfortable).

wrong.bequem: bequem means comfortable, the opposite of what's needed here. Use unbequem.

gaps.correct_explain: After obwohl, the verb goes to the end: obwohl sie manchmal unbequem ist.
